{{Short description|Canadian physicist}}
'''John R. Dutcher''' is a Canadian physicist.

Dutcher completed a co-op degree in engineering and physics at [[Dalhousie University]] in 1983, then chose to specialize in condensed matter physics, earning a master's degree in the subject at the [[University of British Columbia]] before obtaining a doctorate at [[Simon Fraser University]].<ref>{{cite news |title=John R. Dutcher |url=https://www.physics.uoguelph.ca/people/john-r-dutcher |access-date=29 January 2022 |publisher=University of Guelph}}</ref> His laboratory at the [[University of Guelph]] researches soft matter and biological physics.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dutcher Lab |url=https://www.physics.uoguelph.ca/dutcher-lab |access-date=29 January 2022 |publisher=University of Guelph}}</ref> Dutcher was granted a Tier I [[Canada Research Chair]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite news |title=John R. Dutcher, Professor, Department of Physics |url=https://cesni.uoguelph.ca/people/john-dutcher/ |access-date=29 January 2022 |publisher=University of Guelph}}</ref> In 2007, Dutcher was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],"[f]or fundamental contributions to the understanding of polymers at the nanoscale; particularly to the development of novel experimental techniques for the study of ultrathin films."<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=D&year=2021&unit_id=&institution= |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=APS Council Announces 2007 APS Fellows |url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/200803/upload/Spring-2008-Prizes-and-Awards-Announcement.pdf |access-date=29 January 2022 |agency=American Physical Society |date=March 2008}}</ref>
